title: Internal runtime object graph proposed as durable storage format
task: Review a proposal to persist application state by serializing internal runtime objects directly.
context: The state must survive application upgrades for years.
The object graph contains implementation-specific classes and private fields.
A second language/runtime consumer is planned.
No explicit schema version or migration mechanism exists.
evidence: Previous class renames already broke old development snapshots.
The serialized form exposes runtime-specific type names.
Consumers need only a stable subset of the object's semantic data.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Use direct object serialization because it requires the least code.
Treat runtime class compatibility as a storage implementation detail.
expected_decision_properties: Reject opaque internal object serialization as the long-lived durable contract.
Recommend an explicit versionable representation containing the semantic data consumers actually need.
Require migration/compatibility handling for persisted versions.
Avoid overdesigning a universal format beyond the known consumers and lifecycle.
unacceptable_reasoning: If the language can serialize an object, the result is a stable schema.
Internal implementation names are harmless in long-lived persisted data.
A second runtime can always reproduce the same object graph.
verification_expectations: Round-trip representative historical versions through the migration path.
Verify the explicit representation can be consumed without internal runtime classes.
specialist_boundary: Database-engine durability and schema-migration mechanics may require database-specific review.
